claims: Proof attempt (unreviewed, not formalized): for computation trees over F with one input x(kP), arbitrary many equality tests 'register=0?', and L arithmetic nodes per path, N <= 9*2^L - 1 (L >= log2(N+1) - log2 9); tests add at most 2^{L+1}-1 exceptional nodes and no degree growth. Reduces to a generalised RationalSLP partial-agreement lemma (#centres k with k-1,k,k+1 in G is <= 3d).

Proof attempt (unreviewed): first-difference norm bound for the linear target on arbitrary subsets: #{k in A: k+j in A} <= 4d (+1) for 2j != 0; consequently any partition into 2^D classes (arbitrary predicates) with length-L field programs satisfies N <= 40*2^{2D+L}. Not a barrier against bit-extraction algorithms.
Experimental (toy, F_1009, N=60): identities, degree bounds, nonvanishing and tree bookkeeping verified on random instances; no tightness claim.
